none: Bianchi I has no conformal diagram of its own. Each plane of $t$ and one of $x$, $y$ and $z$ is flat in the time $\int c\,dt/a_i$, and where that time begins and ends is up to the free scale factors. For dust each one begins at a finite value at the singularity and runs on without end, so each plane gives the half of Minkowski's diamond that Kasner's planes give, the three alike.
